summary_hint: Tells a processor whose account, the balance, the monthly payment, and whether it is current.

typed_core.name: issuer_name
typed_core.why: identity/source — issuing institution; authenticity

typed_core.name: creditor_or_servicer_name
typed_core.why: identity — the creditor/servicer that owns the account; liability attribution

typed_core.name: customer_or_debtor_name
typed_core.why: identity — the account holder; match to borrower (flattened from person[])

typed_core.name: customer_or_debtor_name_2
typed_core.why: identity — second holder on a joint account

typed_core.name: customer_or_debtor_count
typed_core.why: disambiguator — how many holders, so a bad name split is visible

typed_core.name: account_number_masked
typed_core.why: PII (restricted, pre_masked); identity — account grouping/dedup key

typed_core.name: account_type
typed_core.why: processor — installment vs revolving vs mortgage drives DTI treatment (degraded from enum)
typed_core.prompt_hint: This is a generic account statement — it may be a mortgage, auto, student, credit-card, or utility account; capture account_type verbatim to disambiguate

typed_core.name: statement_date
typed_core.why: identity/recency — which statement this is

typed_core.name: statement_period_start
typed_core.why: disambiguator — period covered, distinguishes two statements for one account

typed_core.name: statement_period_end
typed_core.why: disambiguator/recency — period end

typed_core.name: previous_balance
typed_core.why: processor — opening balance for the cycle

typed_core.name: current_balance
typed_core.why: processor — the liability balance a DTI/reserve review reads

typed_core.name: minimum_or_scheduled_payment
typed_core.why: processor — monthly obligation for DTI
typed_core.prompt_hint: The contractual monthly obligation, not the amount the borrower chose to pay

typed_core.name: payment_due_date
typed_core.why: processor — when the payment is due

typed_core.name: past_due_amount
typed_core.why: processor — delinquency signal

typed_core.name: days_past_due
typed_core.why: processor — delinquency magnitude

typed_core.name: delinquency_or_collection_stage
typed_core.why: processor — collection stage (degraded from enum)

typed_core.name: current_account_status
typed_core.why: processor — open/closed/current/charged-off headline (degraded from enum)

typed_core.name: credit_limit_or_original_amount
typed_core.why: processor — utilization / original loan amount

typed_core.name: payoff_or_settlement_amount
typed_core.why: processor — payoff figure when the account is to be paid off at closing
typed_core.prompt_hint: Distinguish the statement balance from a payoff/settlement amount (payoff includes accrued interest/fees and has a good-through date)

typed_core.name: payoff_good_through_date
typed_core.why: disambiguator — the date the payoff amount is valid through

typed_core.name: property_address
typed_core.why: identity/linkage — links a mortgage/HELOC statement to the subject property (degraded from address)

typed_core.name: loan_number
typed_core.why: identity/linkage — links to the loan file (confidential)

nested_lists.name: transactions_or_activity
nested_lists.shape_reason: a statement's activity can run to dozens of lines; per-field wrapping would risk the 16,384-token ceiling, so a flat row with one source each is the light choice

fields.name: description
fields.pii_note: transaction descriptions may embed PII — apply the transaction-description redactor pattern, not the raw catch-all

rejected.name: issuer_address, issuer_phone, issuer_email_or_url, creditor_contact_information
rejected.reason: contact detail; no rule, no processor use

rejected.name: interest_charged, fees_charged
rejected.reason: cycle detail with no consumer; captured in transactions_or_activity if needed

rejected.name: available_credit
rejected.reason: derivable from credit_limit_or_original_amount minus current_balance; no consumer

rejected.name: statement_period (date_range)
rejected.reason: no date_range coercer; split into statement_period_start/_end

rejected.name: dispute_or_legal_status
rejected.reason: rare; leave to catch-all until a rule needs it

encoding_variations: 'Statement date' vs a 'statement period' range — some issuers give only one; both statement_date and statement_period_start/_end are captured so the period is unambiguous
Account number appears masked as bullet-1234 or XXXX-1234; retain the last-4 verbatim

Balances may be labeled 'New Balance', 'Current Balance', 'Outstanding Principal', or 'Payoff' — the payoff amount is distinct from the statement balance and needs payoff_good_through_date beside it to be trusted
Status may be words ('Current', '30 days late') or a code; days_past_due beside current_account_status disambiguates

open_questions.q: transactions_or_activity shape and inclusion. Item count spans a few (mortgage statement) to dozens (credit card).
options: omit until a rule needs transaction-level data
open_questions.recommendation: flat-row list — token-safe and reusable GEET'S DECISION (LP-438): BUILD IT — LP-437 made nested lists cheap (one declaration + the generic mechanism); the one-list-budget / defer / no-consumer concern is overturned. Build as flat_row; the per-rule consumer is separate follow-up.

open_questions.q: property_address presence. Only appears on secured-account statements (mortgage/HELOC).
open_questions.recommendation: kept as identity/linkage; confirm it is worth the field for the unsecured-account majority, or make it conditional in guidance

open_questions.q: Statement period as two dates vs the catalog's date_range.
open_questions.recommendation: split to _start/_end because there is no date_range coercer; confirm downstream does not expect a single range field

notes: Do not compute or judge delinquency — record the stated status, days-past-due, and past-due amount as printed.
account_number_masked is already registered in _PII_FIELDS (restricted, pre_masked true); no new registration.
Transaction descriptions in the nested list may embed PII — apply the transaction-description redactor pattern, not the raw catch-all.
